result.summary: The environment is a residential street with sidewalks on both sides but lacks marked pedestrian crossings at the visible intersection. A wide, unmarked roadway and sidewalk obstructions like utility poles and construction fencing reduce the overall pedestrian safety and accessibility.

hazards.name: Lack of marked crosswalks
hazards.description: No painted markings to designate a safe crossing point for pedestrians at the intersection.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground intersection area

hazards.name: Sidewalk obstruction
hazards.description: A utility pole is positioned in the middle of the sidewalk, narrowing the clear path for pedestrians and those with mobility aids.
hazards.location_in_image: Left sidewalk foreground

hazards.name: Construction obstruction
hazards.description: Temporary fencing for utility work blocks a significant portion of the sidewalk path.
hazards.location_in_image: Left sidewalk, mid-ground

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental or ladder-style marked crosswalks to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way and increase driver awareness.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions (bulb-outs) to reduce crossing distance, slow turning vehicles, and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Restrict parking near the intersection to improve sightlines for both pedestrians and drivers.

result.summary: The intersection provides basic pedestrian infrastructure including a marked zebra crosswalk, sidewalks, and curb ramps. However, the absence of visible pedestrian-specific signals and the lack of traffic calming measures like curb extensions or a median refuge increase the risk for people crossing the street.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Signals
hazards.description: No dedicated pedestrian signal heads are visible, forcing pedestrians to rely on vehicle traffic lights which may not provide adequate clearance time.
hazards.location_in_image: At the intersection corners

hazards.name: Wide Crossing Exposure
hazards.description: The pedestrian must cross multiple lanes of traffic without a median refuge, increasing exposure to moving vehicles.
hazards.location_in_image: Center of the roadway at the crosswalk

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install dedicated pedestrian signals with countdown timers to improve predictability and safety for crossing.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

result.summary: The environment features a signalized intersection that lacks basic pedestrian infrastructure such as marked crosswalks and functional sidewalks. A large wooden obstruction blocks the narrow paved area along the stone wall, forcing pedestrians into the roadway.

hazards.name: Unmarked Crossing at Signal
hazards.description: A pedestrian signal is present, but there are no painted crosswalk markings to guide pedestrians or alert drivers to the crossing location.
hazards.location_in_image: Center roadway area near the traffic signal pole

hazards.name: Physical Obstruction
hazards.description: A long wooden pole or log is lying across the narrow paved strip adjacent to the stone wall, blocking any potential pedestrian path.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the base of the stone wall on the far side of the street

hazards.name: Sight Line Obstruction
hazards.description: The stone wall and dense vegetation create a visual barrier that may prevent drivers from seeing pedestrians waiting to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Left and center background along the property line

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental-style crosswalk markings to clearly define the pedestrian right-of-way at the signalized crossing.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Installation and Clearance
interventions.description: Remove obstructions and construct a continuous, ADA-compliant sidewalk along the stone wall to separate pedestrians from traffic.

interventions.title: ADA Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Install detectable warning surfaces and curb ramps to provide an accessible path between the sidewalk and the roadway.

result.summary: The intersection features a marked zebra crosswalk and overhead traffic signals, but lacks visible pedestrian-specific signal heads. While sidewalks are present on both sides, a parked van near the crossing creates a visual obstruction for pedestrians and drivers.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: A white van is parked very close to the crosswalk on the left, blocking sightlines between pedestrians and oncoming traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the road, near the crosswalk.

hazards.name: Missing Pedestrian Signals
hazards.description: There are no visible pedestrian signal heads at this signalized intersection, leaving pedestrians to rely on vehicular signals.
hazards.location_in_image: Intersection corners.

interventions.title: Install Pedestrian Signals
interventions.description: Add countdown pedestrian signals to provide clear right-of-way information for people crossing.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the crosswalk to improve visibility for all road users.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to shorten the crossing distance and improve pedestrian visibility.
